'''Robert E. Valett''' (November 22, 1927&nbsp;– November 14, 2008) was an American [[psychology]] professor who wrote more than 20 books primarily focused on [[educational psychology]]. He earned the distinguished psychologist award from the [[San Joaquin Psychological Association]]<ref name="sjvpa.wildapricot.org">{{Cite web|url=https://sjvpa.wildapricot.org/page-1621952|title=San Joaquin Valley Psychological Association – Distinguished Psychologists|website=sjvpa.wildapricot.org|access-date=2017-02-08}}</ref> and was a president of the [[California Association of School Psychologists]].

==Early life and education==
{{more citations needed section|date=February 2017}}
Robert Edward Valett was born in [[Clinton, Iowa]] on November 22, 1927. His father, Edward John Valett, worked for the railroad as a pipe fitter and his mother, Myrtle (née Peterson), was a saleswoman. Valett attended [[Clinton High School (Iowa)|Clinton High School]] while also achieving the rank of [[Eagle Scout (Boy Scouts of America)|Eagle Scout]] in the Boy Scouts of America.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://iagenweb.org/boards/clinton/obituaries/index.cgi?read=211626|title=Valett, Dr Robert Edward|website=iagenweb.org|access-date=2017-02-03}}</ref> During [[World War II|World War 2]], he served in the [[U.S. Navy Medical Corps]]. He then did his undergraduate work at the [[University of Iowa]] and [[George Williams College, Chicago|George Williams College]]. Valett went on to earn an [[Master of Arts|MA]] from the [[University of Chicago]] (1951<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://magazine.uchicago.edu/9708/9708BOBBooks.html|title="Books by Alumni," U of C Magazine, August 1997|website=magazine.uchicago.edu|access-date=2017-02-08}}</ref> ) and an ([[Doctor of Education|Ed.D.]]) in educational psychology from the [[University of California, Los Angeles|University of California in Los Angeles]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.clintonherald.com/archives/dr-robert-edward-bob-valett/article_4a0f962d-2bcf-5193-9ff3-a39f5e40094d.html|title=Dr. Robert Edward (Bob) Valett|newspaper=Clinton Herald|access-date=2017-02-08|language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
Valett was a professor of psychology at [[Orange Coast College]] in [[Costa Mesa, California|Costa Mesa]], Ca., and the [[University of Canterbury]] in New Zealand and taught psychology from 1970 to 1992 at [[California State University, Fresno]] where he was named Professor Emeritus. He authored several books on [[Learning disability|learning disabilities]], [[child development]], [[dyslexia]] and attention disorders/[[Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder|hyperactivity]]. He received the distinguished psychologist award from the San Joaquin Psychological Association in 1982 and served as president of the California Association of School Psychologists from 1971 to 1972.<ref name="sjvpa.wildapricot.org"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.csus.edu/indiv/b/brocks/workshops/casp/general%20session.2.06.pdf|title=CSUS CASP presidents|last=Valett|first=Robert|date=February 7, 2017|website=www.csus.edu/|archive-url=https://archive.today/20170209115547/http://www.csus.edu/indiv/b/brocks/workshops/casp/general%20session.2.06.pdf|archive-date=February 9, 2017|url-status=live|access-date=2017-02-09|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
In 1950, Valett married Shirley Bellman with whom he had five children. He died on November 14, 2008, in [[Fresno, California|Fresno]], California.
